curriculum.title: Grade 9
curriculum.description: Ontario Grade 9 mathematics (MTH1W, de-streamed) for YRDSB learners: practice with varied question styles and guided exploration. Activities support practice, not certification of mastery.

children.title: Manage emotions
children.description: Identify and manage emotions while engaging in mathematics.
children.example: Explain how you feel when a problem is unfamiliar.

children.title: Cope with challenges
children.description: Recognize stress and use strategies for coping with mathematical challenges.
children.example: Explain how you feel when a problem is unfamiliar.

children.title: Persist and stay motivated
children.description: Maintain motivation and perseverance when working through problems.
children.example: Explain how you feel when a problem is unfamiliar.

children.title: Collaborate and communicate
children.description: Build relationships, listen to different mathematical ideas, and communicate respectfully.
children.example: Explain how you feel when a problem is unfamiliar.

children.title: Confidence and self-awareness
children.description: Develop awareness of yourself as a capable mathematics learner.
children.example: Explain how you feel when a problem is unfamiliar.

children.title: Critical and creative thinking
children.description: Think critically and creatively to support mathematical decisions and problem solving.
children.example: Explain how you feel when a problem is unfamiliar.

children.title: Mathematical processes
children.description: Apply the mathematical processes to build understanding and procedural fluency.
children.example: Choose a problem and name the processes you used.

children.title: Making connections
children.description: Connect mathematics to knowledge systems, lived experience, real-life uses and careers.
children.example: Describe where this math appears outside class.

children.title: B1 · Development of numbers and number sets
Development and use of numbers
children.description: Research a number concept and tell a story about its development, use and relevance.
children.example: Tell the story of zero, the Hindu–Arabic numerals, or Indigenous counting systems.

children.title: Number sets
children.description: Describe how subsets of the real numbers are defined and how they are alike and different.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Density, infinity and limits
children.description: Use patterns to explain density, infinity and limits for number sets.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Powers and scientific notation
children.description: Relate the sign and size of an exponent to the value of a power; use scientific notation.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Exponent laws
children.description: Use patterns to develop the exponent laws and simplify numeric and algebraic expressions.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Integers in context
children.description: Use integers to describe location, direction, amount and changes.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Unit fractions and measuring tools
children.description: Use unit fractions and their relationships to other fractional amounts, including measuring tools.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Signs in ratios, rates, fractions and decimals
children.description: Explain how positive and negative signs affect ratios, rates, fractions and decimals.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Operations with fractions and mixed numbers
children.description: Solve problems with positive and negative fractions and mixed numbers.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Rates, percentages and proportions
children.description: Pose and solve problems with rates, percentages and proportions in real contexts.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Development and use of algebra
children.description: Research an algebraic concept and tell a story about its development, use and relevance.
children.example: Tell the story of al-jabr, the equals sign or variables.

children.title: Write expressions to generalize
children.description: Create algebraic expressions that generalize relationships in words, numbers and diagrams.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Compare expressions
children.description: Decide whether expressions are equivalent using concrete, numerical, graphical and algebraic methods.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Simplify expressions
children.description: Simplify expressions using the properties of operations.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Create and solve equations
children.description: Create and solve equations for various contexts and verify the solutions.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Use coding for algebraic concepts
children.description: Use code to show variables, parameters, equations and inequalities.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Decompose problems into steps
children.description: Create code by decomposing situations into computational steps.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Read and alter code
children.description: Read code to predict output, and alter its parameters or constraints.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Compare linear and non-linear relations
children.description: Compare the shapes of graphs to describe rates of change, growth and predictions.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Represent linear relations
children.description: Represent linear relations with materials, tables, graphs and equations.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Compare two linear relations
children.description: Compare two lines y = ax + b graphically and algebraically and interpret their intersection.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Compare characteristics of relations
children.description: Compare the tables, graphs and equations of linear and non-linear relations.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Graph linear forms and regions
children.description: Graph x = k, y = k, x + y = k, x − y = k, ax + by = k, xy = k and their inequalities.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Transform lines
children.description: Translate, reflect and rotate lines y = ax and describe the effect on graphs and equations.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Equations of lines
children.description: Find equations of lines from graphs, tables and materials using slope and y-intercept.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: D1 · Collection, representation and analysis of data
Large data and its implications
children.description: Identify a context with a lot of data and describe the implications of collecting, storing and using it.
children.example: Discuss what data an app collects and why privacy matters.

children.title: Quartiles and box plots
children.description: Represent and analyse one-variable data, including quartiles and box plots.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Scatter plots and models
children.description: Create scatter plots, test regression models with technology and make predictions.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Value of mathematical modelling
children.description: Describe how mathematical modelling informs real-life decisions.
children.example: Name a decision informed by a model.

children.title: Identify a question and information needed
children.description: Identify a question that needs data and decide what information is required.
children.example: Write a question and list the data you need.

children.title: Plan and carry out data collection
children.description: Create a plan to collect data, state assumptions and what may vary, and carry it out.
children.example: Plan a survey or experiment and say what might vary.

children.title: Display and analyse data to build a model
children.description: Choose ways to display and analyse data, considering its nature, context and assumptions, to create a model.
children.example: Choose a graph type and explain why it suits the data.

children.title: Report on a model
children.description: Report how a model answers the question, how well it fits, its limits and predictions.
children.example: Write a short report on what a model tells us and where it fails.

children.title: Development of geometry and measurement
children.description: Research a geometric concept or measurement system and describe its use and relevance to careers.
children.example: Tell the story of the Pythagorean theorem or a traditional measurement system.

children.title: Circle and triangle properties
children.description: Create and analyse designs using geometric relationships and circle and triangle properties.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Units within and between systems
children.description: Solve problems with units within and between measurement systems, including from various cultures.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Changing dimensions
children.description: Show how changing dimensions affects perimeter, area, surface area and volume.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Pythagorean theorem
children.description: Solve right-triangle side problems, including composite shapes.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Volumes of solids
children.description: Use relationships between prism and pyramid volumes and between cylinder and cone volumes.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Financial situations and decisions
children.description: Explain how a past or current financial situation can inform financial decisions.
children.example: Describe a financial situation and what it teaches.

children.title: Appreciation and depreciation
children.description: Recognize situations with appreciation and depreciation and use graphs to answer questions.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Interest, loans and down payments
children.description: Compare interest rates, loan lengths, interest methods and down payments on the overall cost.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Modify budgets
children.description: Modify budgets for changing circumstances and give a rationale.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

suggestedSequence: Number sets, exponent laws, scientific notation, integers, fractions, rates and percentages.
Expressions, equations, code, linear and non-linear relations, lines and transformations.
Quartiles, box plots, scatter plots and the modelling process.
Circle and triangle properties, units, scale, Pythagoras, volumes, interest, depreciation and budgets.
